lines.text: I clean an old high school at night. The janitor before me left one rule, taped inside the supply closet, signed... Walt.
If the bell rings after midnight, don't move. Not one step. Wait until it rings again.
For two years, it never rang. Just me, my cart, and the hum of the vending machines.
Then last Tuesday, at twelve-forty, the bell rang.
Down the hall, every classroom door clicked open... all at once.
Lockers slammed. Sneakers squeaked. Hundreds of footsteps rushed past me, laughing.
But the hallway was completely empty.
Then the footsteps stopped. All of them. Right around me.
And a small voice whispered in my ear... you're late.
I didn't move until the second bell rang, just before dawn.
This morning, the librarian showed me an old yearbook she found in the basement.
The class of nineteen sixty-two. Rows of smiling kids on the bleachers.
And in the back row, holding a mop, stood a man with no smile at all.
The name sewn on his shirt... was Walt.
